newsitem.title: UK: Author Muriel Spark wins British literature prize.
newsitem.headline: Author Muriel Spark wins British literature prize.

text.p: Scottish author Dame Muriel Spark was awarded a prestigious literary prize on Wednesday in honour of her 40-year writing career.
The author of more than 20 novels including "The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie", which was made into a classic 1969 film, was awarded the David Cohen British Literature Prize at a reception in London.
The annual prize, worth 30,000 pounds ($47,840), is given to authors in recognition of a lifetime's achievement.

It also grants 10,000 pounds for the winner to donate to a cause that will encourage young writers. Spark asked that the money be given to her former school in Edinburgh, James Gillespie's High School, on which "The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie" was based.
Actress Maggie Smith won an Academy Award for her leading role in the film. ($1=.6271 Pound)
